caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 337 of 1997
lawyer:
Md Moksudur Rahman, Senior Advocate, instructed by Sharifuddin Chaklader, Advocate-on-Record  ----- For the Petitioners. 
Md Aftab Hossain, Advocate-on-Record  ----- For the Respondents.
parties:
Mobarak Ali ----- Petitioner
Vs. 
Bangladesh House Building Finance Corporation and another ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
"The postal receipts raise the legal presumption of due service and the learned lower tribunal is not right in holding that without the acknowledgement receipts the service could not be inferred. In our view the petitioner has been given reasonable opportunity of self defence and there has been no violation of the service regulations or the principle of natural justice the authority it seems has not done anything unjust to the petitioner. There is scope for adverse interpretation of the irresponsible conduct of the petitioner respondent as found by the Lower Tribunal that the proceedings against the petitioner has been conducted according to the Service Regulations and there has been no illegality or irregularity committed by the authority in proceeding against him and ultimately retiring him from service. The learned Member of the lower tribunal does not appear to have considered the matters in issue in their proper perspective. 

 5. From the materials on record it is seen that show cause notice with the statement of allegations was sent to the addresses of the petitioner available in the record under registered post and that the envelope having not been returned to the sender i.e. the Corporation, the legal presumption is that notices of the proceeding were duly served on the petitioner. That being the position the contention of the learned Counsel that the petitioner was denied of his right to defence and that order compulsorily retiring him was passed without hearing him and consequently there was violation of principle of natural justice has no merit.
